private_dependencies: Amp CLI authentication and Amp internal API/data formats

target: Daycostra Threads Monitor and Workboard architecture
conditions: Do not expose the upstream server beyond localhost; it has no API or WebSocket authentication.
Do not import Amp credential handling, Amp internal API coupling, or Amp thread-file assumptions into Daycostra.
Any reused component must receive an isolated component-level license and dependency assessment.
Reimplement authorization, organization/project tenancy, policy decisions, audit events, retention, and destructive-action controls.
Replace local PTY and filesystem authority with explicit Daycostra runtime contracts.
Use the repository as a source-to-target reference for thread tables, terminal multiplexing, handoffs, relationships, git correlation, and Workboard interaction.
evidence: README.md describes a local React 19 and Node.js application for managing multiple Amp agent threads with table, card, Kanban, terminal, search, handoff, git correlation, skills, MCP status, and WebSocket streaming.
README.md documents Amp-specific storage under ~/.local/share/amp, local SQLite metadata, an Amp internal API client, and an Amp CLI prerequisite.
SECURITY.md states that the server has no API or WebSocket authentication, reads Amp CLI credentials, exposes a full local PTY, and must not be exposed to untrusted networks.
package.json declares Apache-2.0, Node 24, pnpm 10, React 19, Vite 7, better-sqlite3, node-pty, ws, Vitest, and a private package.
The current design is a single-user local development tool rather than a multi-tenant governed production control plane.
